GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 7 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing (it runs the new tests AND `python3 loopfactory.py validate --name podcast`).

OWNED FILES (only these; supervisor, its test, and the fixture are new; the three knowledge files are edited because a runtime change without a map change is drift in this repo):

  departments/podcast/knowledge/subgraphs.json

ARCHITECTURE DECISION THIS IMPLEMENTS (owner-reviewed): the podcast pipeline repo is the
SINGLE execution authority and the only writer of episode state. This department is a
SUPERVISORY plane: it consumes a versioned, content-hashed projection the pipeline
exports, validates it, and escalates gaps. It NEVER schedules pipeline steps, never
decides what runs next, never writes into the pipeline repo. A supervisor that starts
scheduling is the defect (split-brain), not the feature.

THE FROZEN PROJECTION CONTRACT (dag-projection-v1) — both sides of the system build
against this exact shape; do not extend or rename fields:
{
  "schema": "dag-projection-v1",
  "generated_at": "<iso8601 UTC>",
  "source_ref": "<git sha of the podcast repo the projection was built from>",
  "dag_hash": "<sha256 hex of the canonical JSON (sort_keys, compact separators) of the
               steps list below — recomputable by any consumer>",
  "steps": [{"id": str, "requires": [str], "produces": [str], "optional": bool}],
  "episodes": [{
      "episode_id": str, "stage": str,
      "completed": [str],
      "skip_artifacts": {"<step_id>": <episode-skip-v1 artifact dict>},
      "audit": {"complete": bool, "silent_skips": [str],
                "authorized_skips": [str], "invalid_skips": [str]}
  }]
}

BUILD departments/podcast/runtime/dag_supervisor.py, following the established runtime
node pattern — read pipeline_sensor.py (observation appending, argparse, state dir) and
escalate_outbox.py (REPO_ROOT sys.path shim, incident candidates) FIRST and mirror them:

  validate_projection(projection: dict, *, now) -> list[dict]
    Pure. Returns FINDINGS, each {"kind", "episode_id"|None, "detail", "severity"}:
      * schema_mismatch: schema != "dag-projection-v1" (severity critical; no further
        checks — an unknown schema is never partially trusted);
      * dag_hash_mismatch: recomputed sha256 of canonical steps JSON != dag_hash
        (critical — the projection lies about its own graph);
      * stale_projection: generated_at older than 48h relative to `now`, or unparseable
        (unparseable = stale; fail closed);
      * silent_skip: any episode with audit.silent_skips non-empty (critical — this is
        the owner's banned case surfacing);
      * invalid_skip_artifact: audit.invalid_skips non-empty, AND independently: any
        skip_artifacts entry whose recomputed content_hash (sha256 of sorted canonical
        JSON of the artifact minus content_hash) does not match — the supervisor
        re-verifies, it does not take the pipeline's word;
      * unreadable_episode: stage == "unreadable".
    Empty list = healthy.

  sense(projection_path, state_dir, *, now) -> dict
    Loads the projection file, runs validate_projection, appends ONE observation to
    <state_dir>/observations.jsonl in the same shape pipeline_sensor uses (sensor:
    "dag_supervisor", status "ok"|"alarm", evidence = projection path + dag_hash prefix,
    metrics = counts per finding kind), and for a non-empty findings list appends each
    critical finding to <state_dir>/incident_candidates.json in the same structure the
    existing escalation path consumes (READ how escalate_outbox.py / the watchdog write
    and read that file; match it exactly so the existing heal/outbox lane picks these up
    with zero new plumbing).
    A missing or unreadable projection file is itself an ALARM observation with a
    finding {"kind": "projection_missing"} — the absence of the receipt is exactly the
    silence this department exists to catch. Never raise on bad input; the sensor's
    output IS the failure report. Exit codes via main(): 0 healthy, 2 alarm.

  main(): argparse --projection, --state-dir (default departments/podcast/state), --now
  (iso, for tests/cron determinism; default real now).

KNOWLEDGE MAPS: add the dag_supervisor node to procedural-graph.md and subgraphs.json in
the exact format the existing nodes use, and a concept node for "DAG projection
supervision" in concept-map.md tracing to the owner's never-skip requirement (mirror how
existing concept nodes cite interview questions). `python3 loopfactory.py validate
--name podcast` must PASS — that is part of the check.

FIXTURE: departments/podcast/tests/fixtures/dag-projection-sample.json — a healthy
two-episode projection in the frozen shape with a correct dag_hash (compute it for real).

TESTS (departments/podcast/tests/test_dag_supervisor.py; at least 7, tmp state dirs):
 (1) the healthy fixture validates to [] and sense writes an "ok" observation, no
     incident candidates;
 (2) NEGATIVE: flipping one step's "optional" in the fixture without recomputing
     dag_hash yields dag_hash_mismatch (the supervisor recomputes, it never trusts);
 (3) NEGATIVE: an episode with audit.silent_skips non-empty yields silent_skip critical
     AND lands in incident_candidates.json in the consumable shape;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a skip artifact whose detail was mutated after hashing yields
     invalid_skip_artifact even when audit.invalid_skips is empty — independent
     re-verification;
 (5) NEGATIVE: generated_at 3 days old → stale_projection; unparseable generated_at →
     stale_projection (fail closed);
 (6) NEGATIVE: missing projection file → alarm observation with projection_missing,
     exit 2, no crash;
 (7) schema_mismatch short-circuits (no other findings emitted for an unknown schema);
 (8) determinism: same projection + same now → identical findings list.
